name: Dual Contouring and Surface Nets
text:
# Dual Contouring and Surface Nets
## Overview
Dual Contouring and Surface Nets are [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) methods that place a single vertex inside each grid cell intersecting the isosurface, rather than on cell edges as in Marching Cubes [G]. Dual Contouring preserves sharp features by using Hermite data (intersection points and surface normals) to minimize a Quadratic Error Function (QEF) for vertex placement [G]. Surface Nets simplifies this by abandoning gradient data, using the weighted average of edge intersections for vertex placement, resulting in faster computation and smoother topology at the cost of geometric fidelity for sharp features [G].
## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md), where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers [G]. They generate a mesh by placing a single vertex inside each grid cell intersecting the isosurface, rather than on cell edges [G]. The vertex position is determined either by optimizing a quadratic error function using Hermite data (intersection points and normals) or by averaging edge intersection points [G].
## Subtopics

### [Dual Contouring](778-dual-contouring.md)
Dual Contouring is a feature-preserving isosurface extraction method that generates a mesh by placing a single vertex inside each grid cell intersecting the isosurface. It solves the topological ambiguities of Marching Cubes and the loss of sharp features in Surface Nets by using Hermite data (intersection points and surface normals) to minimize a Quadratic Error Function (QEF) for vertex placement. Unlike its siblings, it constructs quadrilateral faces dual to the grid edges where sign changes occur, allowing for sharp crease preservation and non-manifold handling.

### [MLS Projection](823-mls-projection.md)
[MLS Projection](#823-mls-projection.md) is an iterative algorithm that projects a query point onto a surface defined by a set of input points and their associated normals (Hermite data) by fitting a local quadratic function. It solves the problem of robustly estimating the surface position and normal at arbitrary locations in the presence of noise or sparse sampling, which is critical for generating high-quality implicit fields in surface reconstruction pipelines. Unlike standard isosurface extraction methods that rely on grid-based scalar values, MLS Projection operates directly on unstructured point sets, using weighted averages of neighbor projections to converge to the implicit surface. It is distinguished from its siblings in the Dual Contouring family by its reliance on local geometric fitting rather than [global optimization](#5436-global-optimization.md) or grid-based marching, making it suitable for hybrid approaches where grid vertices are projected onto a point-set-defined surface.

### [Surface Nets](921-surface-nets.md)
Surface Nets is an isosurface extraction algorithm that generates a mesh by placing a single vertex inside each grid cell intersected by the surface, positioned at the weighted average of the edge intersection points, and connecting these vertices to form faces. It solves the problem of extracting smooth, watertight triangle or quad meshes from regularly sampled scalar fields or binary volumes. It differs from its sibling [Dual Contouring](778-dual-contouring.md) by abandoning gradient/Hermite data for vertex placement, using only the centroid of edge crossings, which results in simpler topology and faster computation at the cost of potentially lower geometric fidelity for complex features. It differs from [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by producing one vertex per active cell rather than up to one per edge, typically resulting in fewer triangles and a smoother appearance without post-processing.

### [DCX Mesh Extraction via UDF and Marching Cubes](3778-dcx-mesh-extraction-via-udf-and-marching-cubes.md)
DCX extracts a triangular mesh from a BVH structure by computing an Unsigned Distance Field (UDF) on a regular grid, converting it to a Signed Distance Field ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) via [flood fill](#14589-flood-fill-voxelization.md) to determine interior regions, and applying Marching Cubes.

### [Sparse Dual Marching Cubes](3801-sparse-dual-marching-cubes.md)
[Sparse Dual Marching Cubes](#3801-sparse-dual-marching-cubes.md) generates a quad-based mesh from sparse voxel Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) or scalar fields by placing a dual vertex at the center of each active voxel and connecting them across shared isosurface edges. It differs from standard Marching Cubes by producing quadrilateral topology rather than triangles, and from standard Dual Contouring by using fixed voxel centers as dual vertices instead of optimizing vertex positions via linear systems.

### [Screened Poisson Surface Reconstruction](6315-screened-poisson-surface-reconstruction.md)
[Screened Poisson Surface Reconstruction](#6315-screened-poisson-surface-reconstruction.md) (SPSR) is an optimization-based method that fits a surface directly to a single oriented point cloud without prior training. It solves a Poisson equation to reconstruct a watertight manifold mesh, contrasting with marching cubes which may produce non-watertight results and require threshold tuning. It is particularly suited for converting oriented point clouds, such as those derived from 3D Gaussian splats, into explicit triangle meshes for downstream tasks like physics simulation or rendering.

### [Dual Contouring Feature Point Iterative Projection](8388-dual-contouring-feature-point-iterative-projection.md)
This method computes the position of a single vertex (the "feature point") inside a voxel cell for Dual Contouring by iteratively projecting a point onto planes defined by intersecting edges and their normals. It solves the problem of finding a vertex that best represents the intersection of multiple surface constraints within a cell, avoiding the sharp corners or artifacts that can arise from simpler centroid-based placements. It differs from [Dual Contouring](778-dual-contouring.md) by using a fixed-iteration heuristic rather than solving a constrained least-squares system, and from [MLS Projection](823-mls-projection.md) by operating on planar constraints derived from edge intersections rather than local surface fitting.

### [Dual Contouring Edge Normal Calculation](8397-dual-contouring-edge-normal-calculation.md)
This method computes the surface normal for a grid edge intersected by an isosurface by averaging the vertex gradients at the edge's endpoints. It serves as a critical component in Dual Contouring, where accurate normals are required to define the local plane for projecting feature points. Unlike Marching Cubes, which derives normals from cell-centered gradients, this approach leverages the vertex-based gradient information inherent to the dual grid structure to maintain feature preservation.

### [DCx (Dual Contouring over Expanded Cubes)](9342-dcx-dual-contouring-over-expanded-cubes.md)
DCx is an isosurface extraction method designed to reconstruct zero-level sets from neural Unsigned Distance Functions (UDFs), addressing the lack of sign information inherent in unsigned fields. Unlike standard Dual Contouring, which relies on sign changes to identify active cubes and connect vertices, DCx uses an optimization-based strategy to determine active cubes and operates on 2x2x2 voxel blocks (expanded cubes) with a voxel-to-mesh lookup table to handle sparse, irregular active cube distributions and non-manifold structures. It produces single-layer, intersection-free meshes for both manifold and non-manifold inputs without requiring supervision, avoiding the double-layer entanglement and topological errors common in prior UDF extraction methods.
